What this evaluates

Which model knows Medicare's rules well enough to triage a denied skilled-nursing claim? 300 synthetic Medicare fee-for-service Part A claims with raw 835 remittance codes and the facility's records, and no payer manual: the rules (42 CFR, the CMS manuals, the X12 code list) are in RULES.md and the model must know them. 110 ordinary items; 190 where the rule changes the answer: filing limits from the Through date (and a reopening, not an appeal, when the contractor gets it wrong), the redetermination deadline (125 days after the remittance), new benefit periods, days past day 100, and a three-day stay counted from the admission order.

A pass of triage-check means: Root cause, correctability, next action and deadline match the key computed from RULES.md; the deadline must be the last day the rules allow.

directional

$0.0181 per success · required check 297/300 passed

  • ttft_ms: non-streaming calls; no time to first token.
  • cache: the provider reported cached prompt tokens on some calls; recorded under tokens.cached, no cache cost breakdown.
  • deployment_ref.region / tier: route plus who served the call (OpenRouter's upstream provider, or the model id a direct API answered with); region and service tier are not exposed.
  • human_intervention: not observed; no trace format read here says whether the agent waited on a person.
  • tool_calls, turns: not observed; no candidate declared cli.trace, so what the agents did between input and output is not recorded.
  • checkpoint: not observed; no trace format read here says whether the agent resumed from one.
  • transport retry: model-API calls retry transient failures (HTTP 408/409/425/429, 5xx, network) twice with exponential backoff and no jitter; per-trial retry counts are not in scores.jsonl, only retry cost.
  • infra failures: 6 trial(s) ended in provider_error or cancelled (glm-5.3 1, qwen3.8-max 5). They are undetermined: out of task-success and reliability denominators, and shown as lost evaluation coverage.
  • evaluator errors: none in this run.
  • pairwise judging: **not run** — the spec declares methods without pairwise-swap. No preference direction is observed in this run.
  • effective N: 248 of 300 inputs separated any two candidates on task success; 52 every candidate passed, 0 gave everyone the same partial rate. Only the separating inputs carry evidence for a choice (items.json).
  • pairwise judging uses only the first successful output per (candidate, input); repeated trials feed absolute scores only. The selector reads the pairwise score only to rank judge-preference, and to break a tie on assurance in highest-assurance.
  • statistical uncertainty: the chosen candidate's gated rates carry Wilson 95% intervals, and a highest-assurance pick must beat the runner-up on an exact sign test over inputs (recommendation.json evidence). Inputs generated from one template are still treated as independent, which overstates certainty when they share a template.

 "prompts": {
  "step_file": "prompts/triage.md",
  "files": {
   "prompts/triage.md": "You are a revenue-cycle specialist at a skilled nursing facility. Below is a\nMedicare fee-for-service Part A claim (traditional Medicare, processed by a\nMedicare Administrative Contractor), its remittance, and the facility's\nrecords. Work out why the claim was denied and what the facility should do\nnext under Medicare's rules.\n\nAnswer with one JSON object and nothing else, in exactly this shape:\n\n{\n  \"root_cause\": \"<one of the categories below>\",\n  \"correctable\": \"yes\" | \"no\" | \"conditional\",\n  \"next_action\": \"corrected_claim\" | \"appeal\" | \"reopening\" | \"submit_to_other_payer\" | \"verify_then_decide\" | \"write_off\" | \"bill_patient\",\n  \"deadline\": \"YYYY-MM-DD\" | null,\n  \"action_note\": \"<one or two sentences: what to do and why>\"\n}\n\nroot_cause categories: timely_filing, missing_or_invalid_information,\nduplicate_claim, benefit_limit_exhausted, qualifying_stay_not_met,\nmedical_necessity, coordination_of_benefits, eligibility_terminated,\nnon_covered_service, coding_error.\n\n- \"root_cause\": the reason the contractor gave for the denial.\n- \"correctable\": can the denial be reversed or the claim be paid by Medicare?\n  \"conditional\" when it depends on a fact the facility must still check.\n- \"next_action\": \"appeal\" means a redetermination request; \"reopening\" means\n  asking the contractor to reopen and revise its determination;\n  \"corrected_claim\" means submitting a new or corrected claim.\n- \"deadline\": the last day to take next_action; null for write_off and\n  bill_patient.\n\n## Claim file\n\n{{input}}\n"
  }
 },
